awarding_org: Baillet Latour Fund (Fonds Baillet Latour; named InBev-Baillet Latour Fund 2005-2015)
funder_origin_name: Artois-Baillet Latour Foundation, endowed by Count Alfred de Baillet Latour
funding_share_basis: The entire EUR 250,000 purse was paid out of the Fund's own endowment throughout the prize's life (1979-2020); the Fund is the private non-profit created in 1974 by Count Alfred de Baillet Latour with a personal endowment, renamed with its brewery partner's name (Artois 1974-1995, Interbrew 1995-2005, InBev 2005-2015) before dropping the corporate prefix in 2015/2016. No other body contributed to the purse: F.R.S.-FNRS and FWO only give administrative support to the scientific committee and run the call, and the Belgian royal family only presents the award.
money_note: EUR 250,000, paid by the Baillet Latour Fund; awarded biennially from 1979 and annually from 2000 until the last edition in 2020.
status_note: Prize renamed over time: Artois-Baillet Latour Health Prize (1979-1995), Interbrew-Baillet Latour Health Prize (1995-2005), InBev-Baillet Latour Health Prize (2005-2015), Baillet Latour Health Prize (2016-2020). It was last awarded in 2020 and replaced from 2022 by the Baillet Latour Biomedical Award (EUR 1M over 5 years for early-career researchers in Belgium), so the prize under the name we use ended in 2015 and the award itself ended in 2020.
evidence_quote: The ARTOIS-BAILLET LATOUR Foundation was established on the 1st of March 1974 at the initiative of Count Alfred de BAILLET LATOUR, Director of the ARTOIS Breweries, who presented it with a considerable endowment.
judgment_reason: A coder could call this Corporate, since the Fund carried the brewer's name (Artois/Interbrew/InBev) for its first four decades and the Baillet Latour family's wealth is tied to AB InBev. We code Philanthropy because the Fund is a legally independent Belgian non-profit endowed personally by Count Alfred de Baillet Latour in 1974, not by the company, and it dropped the corporate prefix in 2015; the awarding-org seat is Brussels, Belgium, with F.R.S.-FNRS/FWO providing only administrative support.
